messages:
incident-bot: AUTO-PAGE: PagerDuty PD-INC12345 fired for metrics-pipeline -> prometheus scrape failures + log-ingest backlog. 1200 scrapes failing, log queue ~10.2M msgs. Escalation policy: page oncall -> Aisha. https://pagerduty.local/PD-INC12345 :rotating_light:
Aisha (oncall): ACKING. I'm on it, pulling prometheus and kube. joining tty in 2m.
Ken (sre): oncall handoff in 12m if you need to swap. ping me if you want me to take PD.
Aisha (oncall): quick snapshot:
- prom scrape errors: majority from job="exporter-pool" -> 5xx/timeout
- log-ingest consumer lag: topic=redwood-logs-partitioned lag ~2.3M msgs (consumer group: log-ingest-processor)
- SLI visible: metrics API error rate up to 2.4% last 10m
Jorge (eng-runtime): looking at prometheus-scrape-proxy pods, several OOMKilled recently. HPA not scaling because cpu usage below threshold (we have spike in network wait).
Aisha (oncall): running queries:
```
# scrape failure count by job 5m
sum(increase(prometheus_scrape_series_added[5m])) by (job)
# scrape error rate
sum(increase(prometheus_remote_storage_dropped_samples_total[5m])) / sum(increase(prometheus_engine_scrape_duration_seconds_count[5m]))
```
results: exporter-pool shows huge scrape timeouts, many 504s from exporter side.
Ken (sre): can you curl exporter directly from cluster? maybe exporter is rate-limited at nginx/proxy.
Aisha (oncall): yep, from scrape-proxy pod: `curl -sv http://exporter-12.default.svc:9100/metrics` -> gets `HTTP/1.1 429` and `retry-after: 5`. nginx logs show `limit_req` triggered.
Devon (sre-lead): that explains scrape failures. But log backlog suggests downstream consumers struggling too. Is kafka broker healthy?
Jorge (eng-runtime): kafka brokers show normal cpu, but consumer group lag indicates processors stalled. Checking consumer logs now.
Aisha (oncall): mitigation proposal (initial):
1) temporarily increase nginx limit rate on exporter ingress to reduce 429s (patch config)
2) scale scrape-proxy deployment from 3->8 replicas to smooth traffic
3) restart a subset (1/3) of exporter pods to clear hung connections
4) bump log-ingest processor parallelism (kubernetes deployment replicas + increase consumer threads) to shrink backlog
I'll execute 1 and 2 if no objections.
Sam (support): flagging customer impact: we have 5 tickets saying dashboards outdated; support will post status update that telemetry delays are ongoing, not user data loss.
Ken (sre): thumbs on plan. I'll standby for executor role. Recommend rolling restart of scrape-proxy with pre-stop 30s. Also add temporary route to cached KV to reduce cold hits.
Aisha (oncall): applying nginx rate limit patch now -> `kubectl apply -f /ops/runbooks/scrape-proxy/temporary-rate-increase.yaml`
Aisha (oncall): scaling scrape-proxy: `kubectl scale deploy/scrape-proxy --replicas=8 -n monitoring` -> kube accepted.
incident-bot: PD note: Aisha acknowledged; escalation to next-level (Devon) suppressed. PD link: https://pagerduty.local/PD-INC12345/notes
Jorge (eng-runtime): consumer logs show periodic `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError` in log-ingest-processor instance-3. Restarting that pod now and increasing Xmx for the group.
Aisha (oncall): restarted 1 exporter pod and 1 log-processor. Observability after 3m:
- scrape success rate improving from 38% -> 78%
- log consumer lag decreased 2.3M -> 1.1M (still high but trending down)
Devon (sre-lead): good. Please open a follow-up ticket to investigate root cause: why rate-limit + memory pressure coincided. Could be sudden customer query spike + stale config for autoscaler.
Sam (support): posting status: "partial_degradation - metrics delayed and dashboards may show stale data; engineers actively mitigating" to status page.
Aisha (oncall): running extra health checks: `kubectl get hpa -n monitoring`, `kubectl top pods`, prometheus alert eval. HPA for scrape-proxy still below CPU threshold but network TX high; filed a playbook note to adjust metric used by HPA (use request rate instead of cpu).
Ken (sre): recommended follow-ups: add exporter-side circuit breaker, tighten kube pod resource requests so HPA triggers appropriately, add consumer autoscaling by lag.
incident-bot: PD update: manual ack + note added. Incident severity set to SEV2.
Aisha (oncall): 15m after mitigations: scrape success ~95%, log lag  ~340k and decreasing. No PII exposed, only telemetry.
Jorge (eng-runtime): pushed interim change to consumer deployment to 6 replicas and set Xmx higher. Monitoring keep an eye on GC.
Aisha (oncall): I'll keep PD incident open until log lag <50k and scrape stable for 30m. Sam, leave status as ongoing.
Sam (support): will update customers with ETA: "mitigations applied; backlog draining; next update in 30m"
Devon (sre-lead): nice work. After we close, schedule a postmortem focusing on: rate limit thresholds, autoscaler signals, memory hardening for processors, and customer-visible SLI thresholds.
Aisha (oncall): noted — creating incident follow-up in #postmortems with runbook links.
Ken (sre): final check-in: systems look stable at this time. I'll take the PD handoff at 1711010300 if still open.
Aisha (oncall): confirmed. Leaving thread for handoff/watch. Thanks team :thumbsup:
